question: Does removing padded support work make the bounded512 head profitable while retaining full dense dW?
stage: Gate A: packed implementation qualification; prepared, real-model replay not run
intervention: Flatten only valid support entries. Recompute the same selected BMM logits in backward; retain FP32 gradient accumulation and full dense dW output.
controls: Remeasure frozen v01 padded sparse and dense_lp/chunked_lp on identical saved h, support, actions, coefficient vector, dtype and temperature. Only numerically qualified baselines may enter the comparison.
primary_metric: Synchronized wall-clock F+B milliseconds for packed_from_padded, including GPU packing, allocation, full dW zeroing and accumulation, versus the faster numerically qualified dense logprob baseline.
secondary_metrics: CUDA-event milliseconds, prepacked F+B time, packed-to-padded speedup, total and incremental peak allocated memory. Prepacking and input transfer are excluded only from the explicitly labeled prepacked lane.
failure: Numerical failure makes an arm unqualified and prevents timing it. Gate A needs both numerical PASS and the two strict speedup thresholds at bounded512/128. Stop this packed PyTorch recipe on failure; no hidden kernel sweep, model scale-up or optimizer redesign.
independent_unit: The same eight authored diagnostic prompt trajectories as v01. Replaying them is an implementation comparison, not new independent scientific evidence; timing repeats remain technical repeats.
limits: No entropy task, hybrid repair, sparse gradient representation, optimizer integration, full-model backward, RL, end-to-end speedup, novelty or general sparse-kernel no-go claim. Shared-GPU speedups, including a value just above 1, are descriptive and provisional. This new gate does not replace the v01 frozen >=1.10x cross-configuration gate.
